facts.anchor: Then, just when he thought his day couldn’t get much worse, the email he’d sent to his manager bounced straight back.

facts.fact: 公司门禁亮红灯：27 年工龄的通行卡失效，他进不去自己工作了二十七年的大楼。
facts.anchor: His momentary good humour evaporated in seconds as a red light appeared on the reader, instead of the usual flashing green one

facts.fact: HR 男声两次把他叫成「Mr Gravel」，随后以安全为由直接挂断电话。
facts.anchor: I’m sorry, I can give you no information on Mr John Grebble. For security reasons I’m now terminating this call.

facts.fact: 隔着玻璃看同事：构成他二十七年社交宇宙的人，成了比陌生人更陌生的人。
facts.anchor: these were people who had constituted almost his entire social universe for the past twenty-seven years. Suddenly they were all bigger strangers than ever.

facts.fact: 银行职员 Finley 摆出二选一：要么你不是你，要么记录出错了。
facts.anchor: Well, the thing is, sir, that you’re telling me you are Mr John Grebble, but the system is telling me that Mr John Grebble is deceased.

facts.fact: 他想起罪案剧侦探的口头禅：不作假设、不信任何人、核查一切——本章的行动纲领。
facts.anchor: One of them had a mantra: Assume nothing; believe no one; check everything.

facts.fact: 警局问是否有服药、精神病史——受害者反被当成疯子审问。
facts.anchor: And may I ask, Mr Grebble, are you on any medication?

facts.fact: DC Patel 摊牌：警方反而怀疑他冒用死者身份，要他带弟弟与护照来对质。
facts.anchor: The way it appears, you may be using the identity of a deceased person and we need to clarify that.
